newsitem.title: COSTA RICA: Costa Rica seeks new deal with IMF.
newsitem.headline: Costa Rica seeks new deal with IMF.

text.p: Costa Rica is negotiating a new accord with the International Monetary Fund (IMF) after failing to meet targets set in an existing agreement dating from October 1995, Finance Minister Francisco de Paula said Thursday.
"With the new accord, which we aim to have in effect in mid-1997, we will try to reach a fiscal balance in four or five years," de Paula said.
He said talks with IMF officials began last week in San Jose.

Under the old accord, Costa Rica was supposed to limit its fiscal deficit to 0.5 percent of Gross Domestic Product (GDP) in 1996, but de Paula said the deficit would end this year at between 4.5 percent and five percent of GDP.
He said GDP growth in 1996 would be zero and that unemployment would increase, though he gave no figures.

President Jose Maria Figueres is due to announce measures to tackle the government's booming domestic debt, one of its biggest problems, on Dec 16 and is studying privatizing several state-owned firms.
